name: trigger_derived_down
comment: ADR-0042 + ADR-0018 on SQL Server (ADR-0043): one statement-level trigger; the rollback guards on this version's rendering, drops it, and recreates the previous declaration through the dialect. No `triggers` deep expect: SQL Server's stored text renders {new: id} as `inserted`, so the declaration cannot be read back — the guard's MIG-012 comparison on the rendering is the proof that the live trigger is the expected one.

snapshots.sql: update widgets set name = name where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);
update widgets set name = name where id in (select o.id from {old: id} o);

up: create table [widgets] ([id] bigint identity(1,1) primary key, [name] nvarchar(max))

trigger.sql: update widgets set name = name where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

expectTrigger.sql: update widgets set name = name where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

trigger.sql: update widgets set name = name where id in (select o.id from {old: id} o);
